revalidation_triggers: a casting shop supplies process-specific values
a source page or manufacturer guideline changes
the alloy or finishing scope becomes explicit

a later deep-research pass reports a different value for the same finding key

min_castable_wire_diameter_mm.verbatim: Published guidance brackets minimum design thickness at 0.40 mm for general components and 1.0 mm throughout for a general casting recommendation; thinner sections may work depending on geometry and metal flow.
min_castable_wire_diameter_mm.notes: Cross-source bracket, not a consensus and not one shop's accepted band. Morris & Watson states at least 0.40 mm for minimum design thickness and 0.50 mm for broad or flat areas, while Hoover & Strong recommends 1.0 mm throughout but says smaller widths can sometimes cast depending on how far the metal travels. Morris & Watson also warns that finishing can remove 0.10-0.20 mm. Recorded as an uncalibrated research floor only. Sources: https://morrisandwatson.com/casting/cad-design-guidelines and https://cms.hooverandstrong.com/uploads/Casting_Brochure5_2_24_ccfac814e1.pdf. Pass 2 (2026-08-26) independently cites a 0.5 mm general casting-thickness example from Stuller's New Production Standards PDF, sitting inside this bracket -- corroboration, not a new floor. Pass 2's own conclusion is that no authoritative source gives a universal alloy-independent minimum; every published number here, including this bracket, is one supplier's or casting house's own guidance, not a receiving shop's measured process.

attributed_to.name: Formlabs
attributed_to.role: jewelry pattern and casting design guidance

min_prong_base_diameter_mm.verbatim: Formlabs gives 0.5 mm as a minimum for prongs in a structural application; its example uses 0.7 mm for a 2.5 mm side stone and 1.0 mm for an 8 mm center stone.
min_prong_base_diameter_mm.notes: A design example for printed pattern plus casting, not a universal center-prong rule and not a post-finishing measurement. It supports asking how the minimum changes with stone size; it does not calibrate MyJewl's prong floor. Source: https://formlabs-media.formlabs.com/filer_public/17/a1/17a190d9-9a76-4cf5-af12-3d0dda4121dc/formlabs-design-guide.pdf

min_feature_separation_mm.verbatim: Maintain at least 0.20 mm between components such as claws, setting posts and walls.
min_feature_separation_mm.notes: Published CAD gap guidance. Actual investment, feature length, alloy, orientation and finishing may require more clearance. It is not a shop-specific acceptance policy. Source: https://morrisandwatson.com/casting/cad-design-guidelines

min_pinpoint_prong_diameter_mm.verbatim: 0.45 mm minimum prong diameter for pinpoint (melee) prong settings.
min_pinpoint_prong_diameter_mm.notes: This is a MELEE/pinpoint-prong minimum, not a centre-stone prong minimum -- do not compare it against min_prong_base_diameter_mm or MyJewl's 0.600 mm centre-stone reference. Kept as a distinct key for exactly this reason, per the deep-research brief's own warning against generalizing a melee number to a centre prong. From ChatGPT deep-research Pass 1 (modeling pipeline / prongs, seats, and setting), 2026-08-26. Source: https://stuller.scene7.com/is/content/Stuller/DAS/27075240-5d0c-4b5d-88a5-a6bf00ee2785.pdf. Pass 2 (casting/manufacturing, 2026-08-26) independently cites the same 0.45 mm prong figure from a second, different Stuller document (https://stuller.scene7.com/is/content/Stuller/DAS/09b4e2e2-e12e-45f8-a2ed-a4f80104aa9f.pdf) -- two separate Stuller publications agreeing, still one supplier's own CAD guidance and still not alloy- or centre-stone-specific.

min_culet_to_finger_rail_clearance_mm.verbatim: 0.5 mm candidate clearance between the stone's culet and the finger/comfort rail.
min_culet_to_finger_rail_clearance_mm.notes: CAD/CAM design guidance, not a shop's measured or accepted policy for MyJewl's geometry. Nothing today checks a culet-to-rail distance. From ChatGPT deep-research Pass 1, 2026-08-26. Source: https://stuller.scene7.com/is/content/Stuller/DAS/27075240-5d0c-4b5d-88a5-a6bf00ee2785.pdf. Pass 2 independently cites the same 0.5 mm figure from a second, different Stuller document (https://stuller.scene7.com/is/content/Stuller/DAS/09b4e2e2-e12e-45f8-a2ed-a4f80104aa9f.pdf), describing it as a general setting/structure clearance example rather than a wear rule.

min_gallery_rail_spacing_mm.verbatim: 0.4 mm candidate minimum spacing for gallery rail / bearing-adjacent features.
min_gallery_rail_spacing_mm.notes: CAD/CAM design guidance, distinct from min_feature_separation_mm (Morris & Watson's general inter-component gap) -- this one is gallery/bearing-specific. From ChatGPT deep-research Pass 1, 2026-08-26. Source: https://stuller.scene7.com/is/content/Stuller/DAS/27075240-5d0c-4b5d-88a5-a6bf00ee2785.pdf

min_structural_wall_mm.notes: General structural wall, not prong-specific -- the closest MyJewl analogue is basket petal / gallery rail wire, not the prong taper. Not alloy-specific; Pass 2's own conclusion is no universal wall minimum exists by alloy. From ChatGPT deep-research Pass 2 (casting/manufacturing), 2026-08-26. Source: https://stuller.scene7.com/is/content/Stuller/DAS/09b4e2e2-e12e-45f8-a2ed-a4f80104aa9f.pdf

min_internal_wall_mm.notes: Distinct locus from min_structural_wall_mm (external/structural) -- an internal floor or interior wall, e.g. inside a hollowed section. MyJewl does not currently hollow any part, so this has no direct analogue yet. From ChatGPT deep-research Pass 2, 2026-08-26. Source: https://stuller.scene7.com/is/content/Stuller/DAS/09b4e2e2-e12e-45f8-a2ed-a4f80104aa9f.pdf

min_bridge_width_mm.verbatim: 1.5 mm width x 1.2 mm height bridge/rail example.
min_bridge_width_mm.notes: Split into two keys (width, height) because a bridge cross-section needs both axes and the schema's finding is one scalar/range per key -- see min_bridge_height_mm for the paired figure. From ChatGPT deep-research Pass 2, 2026-08-26. Source: https://stuller.scene7.com/is/content/Stuller/DAS/09b4e2e2-e12e-45f8-a2ed-a4f80104aa9f.pdf

min_bridge_height_mm.verbatim: 1.5 mm width x 1.2 mm height bridge/rail example.
min_bridge_height_mm.notes: Paired with min_bridge_width_mm -- the same one Stuller example, split across two keys because the finding schema is one scalar/range per key. From ChatGPT deep-research Pass 2, 2026-08-26. Source: https://stuller.scene7.com/is/content/Stuller/DAS/09b4e2e2-e12e-45f8-a2ed-a4f80104aa9f.pdf

min_stone_to_stone_spacing_mm.notes: Relevant to pave/side-stone schedules (trilogy, pave accents), not the solitaire centre stone. MyJewl's live catalog includes a pave/trilogy reference combination (Goal 0007) with no such spacing check today. From ChatGPT deep-research Pass 2, 2026-08-26. Source: https://stuller.scene7.com/is/content/Stuller/DAS/09b4e2e2-e12e-45f8-a2ed-a4f80104aa9f.pdf
